A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIDS research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched reliably, including material relocated in v2.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original synthetic regression and classification experiments, plus evaluations on CIFAR-10-C, Celeb-A, and three UCI datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their results, and adds method-specific runtime measurements in Appendix E.5, Table 5.

M1.justification: The adaptive prior, amortized Gaussian posterior, pretrained embeddings, synthetic-environment sampling, objectives, and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. The added normalizing-factor paragraph documents implementation without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic tasks, CIFAR corruptions, Celeb-A attribute shifts, and Boston, Concrete, and Wine regression datasets. The runtime table covers existing experiments without adding a dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: DUE, SNGP, and DUL remain the comparison methods throughout the retained experiments and also appear in the new runtime table. The newly cited Hypernetworks and Bayesian model-agnostic meta-learning papers are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Table 5 extends comparative evaluation to execution time, specifying seconds or minutes and maxima across CIFAR-C corruptions and Celeb-A tasks. Existing predictive metrics, splits, preprocessing, architectures, and training budgets remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix E.5 adds a computational-efficiency analysis comparing costs on smaller models and image models, supported by Table 5. Existing analyses of prior adaptation and sensitivity to the regression shift parameter remain unchanged; no new component ablation is introduced.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 newly identifies tabulated performance summaries as means and standard deviations across replicates; v1's Table 1 does not define its parenthesized dispersion values. Existing repetition counts and uncertainty displays are retained, without evidence of additional runs, seeds, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Predictive results in Table 1 and Figures 5–7 and 9 are unchanged. Table 5 adds runtime results: for example, VIDS versus DUE takes 67.160 versus 39.900 seconds for linear regression, but 2.516 versus 7.447 minutes for the CIFAR-C maximum. These are new cost measurements, not improved predictive scores.

T1.justification: The numbered mathematical development, Proposition 3.1, Proposition B.1 and its proof, Remark B.2, and support-mismatch discussion are unchanged. The new implementation approximation does not revise the formal prior definition or add a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about adaptive priors, amortized inference, synthetic environments, and uncertainty estimation under covariate shift. The runtime discussion does not redefine the main contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix E.5 newly attributes higher small-model costs to per-environment optimization and an advantage on larger models to restricting variational inference to the prediction layer. Earlier interpretations remain intact. The checklist's reference to limitations in the conclusion does not correspond to an actual added limitations discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds an explanation of approximating the continuous-response normalizing factor. Appendix E.5 replaces reliance on broad timing bounds with additional per-method, per-dataset timings on the already specified hardware. Software versions, hyperparameter tables, and the promised future public code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ha et al. (2016), Hypernetworks, and Yoon et al. (2018), Bayesian model-agnostic meta-learning. A brief related-work addition contrasts shared parameter priors with VIDS's covariate-adaptive prior; the broader positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds brief related-work and implementation passages, a runtime subsection, acknowledgments, and a NeurIPS checklist, and updates the conference footer. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are unchanged; the longer document is not an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5, relocates Algorithm 1, and adjusts page layout. Figure 2 gains a 1:N plate label but loses red arrow highlighting while its caption still describes red arrows. Figure 3's caption is expanded; the existing result graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix E.5 and Table 5 make computational tradeoffs assessable where v1 supplied only broad timing bounds. Added implementation and statistical explanations provide further limited transparency. These gains leave the main scientific evidence unchanged and are tempered by unclear notation in the new normalizer expression, Figure 2's color-caption mismatch, and the checklist's unsupported reference to limitations in the conclusion.
